answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with slashable identity bonds: every agent locks a refundable deposit before it can transact, like a pearl kept in escrow. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real capital, and the bond is ferrous - it sticks to the agent history, so a bad actor that burns one identity loses its deposit and its accumulated trust. Honest agents that complete verified work earn saffron-marked reputation credits that lower their future bond, so genuine participants get cheaper while attackers keep paying full price for each new fake.
